clue.text: Mosaic piece from Hardy's novel period

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Thomas Hardy's novel, known as Tess
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A fragment of mosaic seemingly lifted from a Victorian novel's era.
explanation.definitionFit: A small square tile of stone or glass used in mosaic work goes by this Latin-derived name.

clue.text: Time of payment is sweet

parts.note: taken as written
a fee is a payment for a service

explanation.surface: The moment you get paid feels sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter is a kind of sweet, the British word for candy.

clue.text: Predicament? Economise

definitions.meaning: to be in an awkward fix
to ... by or ... and save is to economise hard

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: an awkward fix, and the verb for saving every penny.

clue.text: End of the ideal solution to the lot

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from the word the

parts.note: the very thing is the phrase for exactly what is needed, an ideal solution

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the perfect answer to the whole business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the very thing' is an idiom for exactly what is wanted; drop the space and add the E from 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lot is a colloquial phrase for all of something, the whole amount.

clue.text: Suburban villa's contribution to 9

indicators.note: the possessive is read as has: the two words have the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A suburban villa gives something towards the local forge.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is FORGE, so the definition is something a forge needs; the answer runs across 'suburbAN VILla'.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron block on which a smith hammers metal is the central piece of equipment of a smithy.

clue.text: I work with 22 a long way before I go wrong, putting last first

parts.note: far means a long way

indicators.note: the final letter of the little phrase is moved round to its front

parts.note: to err is to go wrong

explanation.surface: A worker explains a winding sequence of going far and going astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting last first' moves the final R of the I-plus-error piece to its front. 22 is the lucky iron items a smith fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith who shoes horses is the tradesman who fits horseshoes.

clue.text: Tries moving into sunny part of Brittany

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for sunny

parts.note: fine weather is sunny weather

indicators.note: the letters of the word tries are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to relocate to a sun-blessed corner of north-western France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns TRIES into ISTER, which goes 'into' FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French département at the western tip of Brittany bears this name, meaning land's end.

clue.text: But not that unusual for roast beef?

definitions.text: But not that unusual for roast beef?

parts.words: But not that unusual for roast beef?
parts.note: the word for unusual is also how many like their roast beef cooked, so the description is not unusual there

explanation.surface: A comment that bloody roast beef is common enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means uncommon, yet also describes beef cooked lightly and still red, a very common order.

clue.text: Pinter's work in self-disclosure is courageous

indicators.note: the shuffled playwright's name goes inside the identity letters

parts.note: showing your ID card discloses who you are, your identity

indicators.note: the playwright's name is worked into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A Harold Pinter play about revealing oneself is called brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges PINTER as NTREPI, which goes 'in' ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and bold, the word is a direct synonym for brave or courageous.

clue.text: Warning of danger when Spooner was the Tory leader

indicators.note: Spooner was the clergyman famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: the clue's was the leader means led
the Tories are the party of the political right

explanation.surface: An alarm sounded when the Reverend Spooner headed the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was the Tory leader' reads as LED RIGHT; swap the L and R sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A red traffic signal or lamp is the standard signal to stop because of danger.

clue.text: Seek food rejecting article as fake

indicators.note: the article is thrown out of the word for seeking food

parts.note: to forage is to search for food
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for food casts aside a counterfeit item.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge a signature or banknote is to fake it, to counterfeit it.

clue.text: Worshipped ere Advent came about

indicators.note: something that came about turned round, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Something was revered before the Christmas season arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To venerate is to revere or worship, so the past tense matches worshipped.

clue.text: Last words of Omar: the pessimist has half one

definitions.meaning: FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam ends 'Turn down an ...!'
a pessimist sees the glass as half empty rather than half full

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase closes the Rubaiyat, and the pessimist's tumbler is proverbially half this way.

clue.text: Jean's tribe?

parts.note: jeans of a famous brand, and one of the twelve tribes of Israel, share the name

explanation.definitionFit: One of the tribes of Israel shares the name of a well-known brand of denim jeans.

clue.text: Apparent demands — so be silent

indicators.note: the words are required to be reworked, demands read as calling for change

explanation.surface: A seeming order to hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensible means seeming or professed on the surface, the same as apparent.

clue.text: Tool for 9 with operator in London

parts.note: a hammer is the tool used at a forge
a smith is the person who operates a forge

explanation.surface: A forge's tool and its worker are found in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: HAMMERSMITH is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: This district lies in west London, so it is a place in the capital.

clue.text: Art of warm cooked peas

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are messed about, as in cooking the books

explanation.surface: The craft of warm cooking applied to peas.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of large dried peas, used for mushy peas, carries this name.

clue.text: Golden Bough's ending first has tree turned to ice — nearly awful!

indicators.note: the letter from Bough is put before the word for golden
the end of the word Bough is its final letter

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: the tree's name is turned backwards

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree

indicators.note: the word ice is nearly complete, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: In Frazer's Golden Bough a tree freezes over, a dreadful scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes RIF from FIR; 'nearly' cuts ICE to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrific and awful are synonyms for something dreadful or shocking.

clue.text: Spell Shah Jahan's city with many a starry figure

parts.note: a hex is a spell or curse
Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A curse on the Mughal emperor's city brings a star-shaped symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pointed star formed by two overlapping triangles is this figure.

clue.text: A once new building block of sea air (that let down Bingo in the Goodwood Cup)

definitions.text: sea air (that let down Bingo in the Goodwood Cup)

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over afresh

parts.note: a breeze block is a light building block

explanation.surface: A breezy coastal wind, plus a dig at a Wodehouse character's losing racehorse bet.
explanation.walkthrough: In P G Wodehouse's stories Bingo Little lost money backing a horse of this name at Goodwood, an English racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing in off the sea is literally a sea air, and was also a racehorse's name.

clue.text: Transatlantic city in Atlantic country

indicators.note: the city goes inside the ocean's nickname

parts.note: the pond is jocular slang for the Atlantic Ocean
LA, Los Angeles, is a city across the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.surface: An American city found in a nation by the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: This central European nation is a country.

clue.text: Comic Arthur eating hard fruit from tree

indicators.note: the comedian's name takes in the letter for hard

parts.note: Arthur Askey was a British comedian of radio and TV
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A comedian munching on tough fruit picked from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Askey was a much-loved British comedian of the mid-20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged seed of an ash tree is called by this name, a fruit of the tree.

clue.text: See 24
Lucky products of 9 for 4 ft?

parts.note: a forge makes these lucky charms for a horse's four feet

explanation.definitionFit: Iron shoes for a horse's hooves are made at a forge and hung up for luck.

clue.text: Cut covering page division

indicators.note: the word for cut wraps round the page letter

parts.note: a slit is a cut

explanation.surface: A cut over a page divides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A split is a division or rift, as in a split within a party.

clue.text: The Guardian is going to study the literate

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as we, so we will is we'll
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: The newspaper promises to examine those who can read.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in the Guardian, which speaks of itself as 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-read describes someone widely educated through books, a sense close to literate.

clue.text: 9's European air backed with less than total recall

parts.note: 9 across is FORGE

indicators.note: the German word is put backwards

parts.note: Luft is the German for air

explanation.surface: A smithy's atmosphere, backed up, leaves someone unable to remember everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone whose memory fails them has incomplete recall, which is what forgetful means.

clue.text: Number in reverse like operator in 9

indicators.note: the number goes inside the word for reverse

parts.note: to back is to reverse, as a car
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A number in reverse resembles the forge worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The operator in a forge is a blacksmith.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith works iron, the black metal, so the word describes the smith at a forge.

clue.text: Where Arthur kept appointment with fate?

parts.note: someone who kept an appointment came along
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: King Arthur's seat, where he met his destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: King Arthur held court at this legendary castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary court of King Arthur is the place where he lived.

clue.text: Flower ill-used within the jurisdiction of the war god

definitions.text: the jurisdiction of the war god

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the river

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Tay in Scotland

indicators.note: ill-treated letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A bloom mistreated under the rule of Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill' shuffles the second half of 'ill-used'; the Tay is Scotland's longest river. The weekday is named after Tiw, the Germanic war god.
explanation.definitionFit: This weekday is named for Tiw, the Germanic god of war, so it is his day.
